owner_direction.quote: 魔法陣の挟み込み以外はいい。魔法陣の挟み込みは半円の形の両脇がださすぎる。もとの表現だとぶつ切りにはなってたけど見た目はよかったろ。あの切り方でエフェクトだけ今回のにしろよ。
owner_direction.meaning: Everything else in #112 is approved. The semicircular ends on both sides of the live stream between the seals are far too ugly; the original abruptly cut stream looked good. Use that cut and take only the effect (the current black-blood ScarletInk material).
owner_direction.original_expression: 0.3.29-0.3.67: CrimsonEnergy's PortalBeam slab, cut flat at the stream ends (the seal centres), seals drawn under it. Never a round cap (0.3.68-0.3.80 had 140 px caps past the seals, 0.3.83 caps stopping on the seal centres). Source of the finding: the history study of the crossflow (git-ignored, .local/crossflow-history), not committed.

decision.cut: flat, on the stream ends (Reach): the seal centres in the open, the wall at a wall. Not at the seal ring's inner edge (a lens-shaped gap and an invisible hit past the picture).
decision.seals: under the forecast while charging (age < Fire); over the live stream and vapor from Fire until they fade (age < End). Reasons, from real-size frames of both orders: against a wall the held seal (SealInset 52 px) is almost entirely hidden by the opaque black band when drawn under it (only its top and bottom 45 px show) and the crossflow reads from one side; in the open the band paints over a seal's inner half, which the original's white slab could afford but a black band cannot; over the stream a whole ring frames each cut, the 1 px cut sits under the seal's pattern, and it matches the order the owner saw on #112's page. One list (sealsOver) in DrawTrackingBeams reverts it if the owner prefers 0.3.91's order.
decision.ends_and_front: flat. A softened front would need the shader (ScarletInk's VS and PS read no vertex colour); the original's front fade was 5-12 px, practically a cut.
decision.collision: unchanged capsule, protocol 80. The band lies over the whole capsule, tangent to it on the end-centre lines, and inside the forecast band; only the four corners the round ends cut off (1 end = (2 - pi/2) r^2 = 8,412 px^2 at r = 140, 58 px at most) are inked without hurting, the safe side. A flat-band hitbox would change shared geometry (protocol 81, a wall body would have to leave the line by 161 px instead of 93 px).
decision.drawing: the existing clip: ScarletInkStroke draws the band over the capsule's span (hi = max(A.x, B.x) + r, lo = min(A.x, B.x) - r) with the shader's own segment as the band and the quad stopping at both ends, so ScarletInk.fx, ScarletInk.fxc, compiled.json and the 14 pinned hashes are untouched. A shader 'cap' parameter was rejected (hashes and G11's reference would move; at most 7/255 different).
